findings.claim: Scope 1: **Credits and notices.** This is a non-commercial post, not endorsed by FRED, the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis or any publisher of these data.
findings.evidence: sources/fred_legal_notices.txt:179 bars suggesting FRED or the St. Louis Fed endorses the user's conclusions and :225 bars implying endorsement; naming them in a disclaimer is attribution, not barred by :411. Nothing FRED requires for a non-commercial blog is missing (citation, via FRED, notice kept; FRED Graphs and API notices not triggered).

findings.claim: Scope 2: [[published] metaDescription] On the S&P 500's worst 5 percent of days from 2020 to 2026, Bitcoin's average log return was minus 4.4 percent.
findings.evidence: Recomputed: 1,605 daily returns, k = ceil(80.25) = 81, no ties at the cutoff; Bitcoin mean log return -4.3912% (CI -5.95 to -2.83); plain mean -4.08%, so 'average log return' cures r5:item:19.

findings.claim: Scope 3: [[published] alt:sh-2-safe-haven-test.png] Thick bars mark the averages and thin bars their 95% confidence intervals.
findings.evidence: make_charts.py:126 draws the average as a horizontal line (lw=3), :127 the 95% CI as a vertical line (lw=2); same strip() for all three panels; PNG agrees.
findings.fix: Clarity: 'Thick horizontal bars mark the averages and thin vertical bars their 95% confidence intervals', since thick and thin differ only by line width 3 against 2.

findings.claim: Scope 4: [[published] alt:sh-3-episodes.png] Horizontal bar chart of each asset's largest fall between the S&P 500's high and its low, in the three S&P 500 falls of 15% or more since 2020.
findings.evidence: Exactly three S&P 500 falls of 15% or more by the episode rule (33.92%, 25.43%, 18.90%; next largest 9.6%); bars are max_fall from peak to trough on S&P trading days (build_analysis.py:274-275).
findings.fix: Narrowed 'each asset's' to 'Bitcoin's and the S&P 500's', the two assets drawn (gold is not on this chart).

findings.claim: Scope 5: [[published] alt:sh-3-episodes.png] Bitcoin fell further in each: 49 percent against 34 across the 24 S&P 500 closes from 2020's high to its low, 61 against 25 across the 196 closes of 2022's, and 22 against 19 across the 35 of 2025's.
findings.evidence: Numbers hold (24/196/35 closes; 48.88 v 33.93, 61.01 v 25.43, 22.40 v 18.90) but the round 5 fix dropped the noun 'fall': '2020's high' literally means calendar 2020's high (3,756.07 on 31 Dec 2020), not the episode high (3,386.15 on 19 Feb 2020); '2025's' likewise points at 24 Dec 2025.
findings.fix: 'across the 24 S&P 500 closes from the 2020 fall's high to its low, ... the 196 closes of the 2022 fall, ... the 35 of the 2025 fall'.

findings.claim: Scope 6: [[published] alt:sh-4-rolling.png] Line chart of the correlation of log changes in calendar-month averages with the S&P 500 over rolling 24-month windows ending January 2022 to April 2026.
findings.evidence: build_analysis.py:284-295 averages over each month's S&P trading days; 76 months, 75 log changes; 24-change windows end 2022-01 to 2026-04 (52 per asset); on month-end changes Bitcoin's range would be 0.34 to 0.61, so the wording cures r5:item:30.

findings.claim: Scope 7: [[published] alt:sh-4-rolling.png] Bitcoin's stays between 0.29 and 0.60; gold's ranges between minus 0.29 and 0.49.
findings.evidence: Bitcoin min 0.2904 (2024-10), max 0.5967 (2024-04); gold min -0.2942 (2025-10), max 0.4930 (2024-03). With calendar-day averages Bitcoin's max would print 0.59, and the post never stated the averaging days.
findings.fix: Method notes now state: 'The S&P 500's and Bitcoin's monthly averages are taken over each month's S&P 500 trading days; gold's is the World Bank's monthly average.' (build_analysis.py:285 docstring).

findings.evidence: True in time order (max 2024-03 before min 2025-10) but invites the start-to-end reading refuted in r5:item:31 for the alt (the line starts at 0.22, ends at -0.13), and the template depended on max preceding min.
